summary: Chevron's global headquarters sits not in Houston or downtown San Francisco but here, in a master-planned East Bay suburb tucked against the western slopes of the San Ramon Valley — a detail that reshapes how you think about the place. That corporate anchor, joined by AT&T's West Coast division offices and a cluster of other firms along Bollinger Canyon Road, means San Ramon functions as a genuine employment node rather than a pure bedroom community, though the I-680 corridor still funnels heavy commute traffic toward Walnut Creek and the Bay. The median household income tops $197,000, yet with homes priced at a median of $1.36 million — roughly a 6.9-to-1 price-to-income ratio — buying still demands significant capital even at that income level; rents near $2,900 absorb a more modest share. The geography is the quiet reward: the valley floor gives way to golden-grass ridgelines that frame Mount Diablo to the northeast, and an extensive Iron Horse Regional Trail corridor threads through town, offering a paved, car-free route for walking and cycling that connects to neighboring cities. With 269 sunny days worth of mild highs averaging 69°F and lows rarely dipping below the upper 40s, evening walks are a year-round option. The tradeoff is legible from any hilltop: a strikingly orderly landscape of subdivisions and office parks that delivers comfort and convenience but trades away the kind of idiosyncratic, walkable downtown energy found in older Bay Area cities.
